High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri R.P. Yadav - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Amit Pandey - Government Advocate for the responde

Heard on I.A. No.18673/2025, second application under Section 430(1) of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (U/S 389(1) of Cr.P.C. 1973) for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.
His first application was dismissed for want of prosecution vide order dated 04.10.2024.

Appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 366 of IPC read with Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for Life and fine of Rs.3,000/- and Section 376(2) of IPC read with Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act along with Section 4 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for life and fine of Rs.5,000/-respectively, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the trial Court has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.
He further submits that there are so many contradiction about the age of the prosecutrix.
He also submits that there is no medical evidence given by the doctors or there is no medical test conducted by the prosecution.
He further submits that prosecutrix is a consenting party.
He also submits that there is delayed in FIR for twenty five days.
Appellant has no previous criminal history.
The appellant has already undergone more than 8 years and 05 months of actual incarceration.
This appeal is of the year 2018 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.
Appellant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.
Learned counsel for the State on the other hand has opposed the application for suspension of sentence and supported the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant can be considered.
Accordingly, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the aforesaid I.A. is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 22.01.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
 (VIVEK KUMAR SINGH) (AJA  JUDGE   NP Rampal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186050990/
